title: Working on adding the first boss fight to my game with Grok
author: same_vibes
selftext:
Still quite work-in-progress but a little glimpse at a boss fight I've been adding to my game Crypt Raiders. Been using this as an excuse to test out Grok 4.5 in Cursor and so far been finding it working really well in this existing codebase and overtaken Composer as my primary model.



The main meat of the game is fighting your way through zombie hordes in labyrinth-like graveyards. Aligned with that the mechanics of this boss take on that of a Minotaur-like raging bull.

  
One of the next things I want to do is work on getting Grok to create a level editor so I can customise the level design here, since normal levels are all procedurally generated, and prompting every little change is a bit tedious. Will share an update as I get it more polished!

comments.author: AxiosXiphos
comments.body: Why Grok? Chatgpt Sol is cheap and far far better.

replies.author: same_vibes
replies.body: I like to try all models, and am using Sol on some other projects. It's a benefit that Grok is now included in the auto/first party usage pool for Cursor, so it's quite economical right now.

replies.author: same_vibes
replies.body: So far feeling like a good new workhorse over Composer in Cursor and haven't found anything that Grok has particularly struggled with. Fast mode rips. It feels to me on par or maybe better than GPT 5.5 or Opus 4.8. But I haven't spent an equal amount of time yet with GPT 5.6 or Fable to compare there.
